title_en: Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Implementation of the Civil Procedure Law (for Trial Implementation) in Economic Adjudication
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Opinions on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Civil Procedure Law (for Trial Implementation) in Economic Trials

(September 17, 1984)

1. Jurisdiction Issues

(1) Territorial Jurisdiction over Economic Contract Cases

In accordance with Article 23 of the Civil Procedure Law (for Trial Implementation), an action arising from a contract dispute shall be filed with the people's court of the place of performance of the contract or the place where the contract was concluded. The place of performance of the contract refers to the place where the obligations stipulated in the contract are performed, generally the place where the subject matter of the contract is delivered. The place where the contract was concluded refers to the place where the contract is signed. In an economic contract case, if the plaintiff files a lawsuit with the people's court of the place of performance of the contract, that people's court shall accept the case in accordance with the law; if one of the plaintiff or the defendant is located at the place where the contract was concluded, the people's court of that place may also have jurisdiction. Where two or more people's courts have jurisdiction, the plaintiff may choose to file a lawsuit with one of those people's courts in accordance with Article 31 of the Civil Procedure Law (for Trial Implementation).

Article 29 of the Civil Procedure Law (for Trial Implementation) provides that if it is difficult to implement Article 23, then jurisdiction shall be exercised by the people's court of the place where the sued entity is located, in accordance with Article 20. The circumstances referred to as "difficult to implement Article 23" mainly include: (1) the subject matter is located in the place where the sued party is based, and it is truly difficult for the people's court of the place of performance of the contract or the place where the contract was concluded to conduct inspections, appraisals, or take preservation measures; (2) the contract was concluded at a place other than the location of the litigation parties and the place of performance of the contract, and it is truly difficult for the people's court of the place where the contract was concluded or the place of performance to exercise jurisdiction.

(2) Level Jurisdiction over Economic Dispute Cases

Regarding level jurisdiction over economic dispute cases, in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Civil Procedure Law (for Trial Implementation), it may be determined by considering the subordinate relationship of the litigation entity, the amount of the subject matter in dispute, and the complexity of the case: for litigation entities subordinate to a prefecture or a city under the jurisdiction of a province (including the prefecture/city level itself), the case shall generally be tried at first instance by a basic people's court, but if the amount of the subject matter is relatively large and the case is relatively complex, it may also be tried at first instance by an intermediate people's court; for litigation entities subordinate to a province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government, the case shall generally be tried at first instance by an intermediate people's court, but if the amount of the subject matter is relatively small and the case is relatively simple, it may also be tried at first instance by a basic people's court; cases of significant impact within a province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government shall be tried at first instance by a higher people's court. As for foreign-related economic dispute cases, they shall all be tried at first instance by an intermediate people's court. Cases involving compatriots from Hong Kong and Macao and their enterprises or organizations shall generally also be tried at first instance by an intermediate people's court, but in locations where there are many such cases, for cases where the amount of the subject matter is relatively small and the case is relatively simple, with the approval of the higher people's court, they may also be tried at first instance by a basic people's court.

2. Litigation Participants

(1) Parties

In accordance with paragraph 2 of Article 44 of the Civil Procedure Law (for Trial Implementation), enterprises, institutions, government organs, and organizations may serve as litigation parties.

During the litigation process, if an enterprise is merged or closed, the litigation parties shall be changed promptly. If an enterprise is merged, the new enterprise after the merger shall serve as the litigation party; if an enterprise is closed, its supervisory unit or the liquidator (unit) shall serve as the litigation party.

Individual business operators, rural specialized households, and rural commune members may also serve as litigation parties in economic contract cases. Cooperative economic organizations that have obtained business licenses from the administrative department for industry and commerce may participate in litigation as independent litigation subjects.

(2) Legal Representatives

The legal representative must be the principal administrative person in charge of the enterprise, institution, government organ, organization, or other economic organization. There are three main situations: first, the principal administrative person holding the substantive position, such as the factory director of a factory, the chairman of a company, or the manager of a company without a board of directors; second, if the entity has no substantive principal administrative person, the deputy person presiding over the work, such as the deputy factory director or deputy manager, may serve; third, if there is no clearly designated principal or deputy position, the administrative person presiding over the work shall serve. No other person of the entity may serve as the legal representative.

(3) Litigation Agents

The method for a party to entrust a litigation agent to act on its behalf in litigation is provided in Article 50 of the Civil Procedure Law (for Trial Implementation). In addition to entrusting a lawyer, the legal representative may also entrust any other person permitted by the people's court to serve as a litigation agent; other litigation subjects may also entrust litigation agents in accordance with the law.

(4) Third Parties

The third party referred to in Article 48 of the Civil Procedure Law (for Trial Implementation) is limited to persons who have an independent claim to the subject matter in dispute between the parties, or who, although having no independent claim, have a legal interest in the outcome of the case. After the parties have initiated the lawsuit and before the people's court renders a judgment, the third party may apply to participate in the litigation or be notified by the people's court to do so. A third party with an independent claim who participates in the litigation enjoys the rights and bears the obligations of a plaintiff. If the people's court's judgment holds a third party without an independent claim liable for economic obligations, such third party shall be permitted to appeal to protect its own lawful rights and interests.

If a third party did not participate in the litigation at first instance, it may apply to participate in the litigation at second instance to protect its own lawful rights and interests. For a case in which the court of second instance permits a third party to participate in the litigation, if no settlement agreement can be reached through mediation, the court shall issue a ruling, set aside the original judgment, and remand the case for retrial.

3. Service

When a mediation document in an economic dispute case is served, if the party refuses to accept it, according to Article 102 of the Civil Procedure Law (for Trial Implementation), it shall be deemed as repudiation before service, and the court shall proceed to trial; it shall not be handled according to Article 70 of the Civil Procedure Law (for Trial Implementation).

4. Compulsory Summons

Article 76 of the Civil Procedure Law (for Trial Implementation) provides that if a defendant who must appear in court, after being lawfully summoned twice by a summons, fails to appear without justifiable reasons, the people's court may issue a compulsory summons. For cases with clear facts and reliable evidence, a default judgment may be rendered in accordance with Article 113 of the Civil Procedure Law (for Trial Implementation).

5. Filing of Lawsuits and Acceptance of Cases

(1) Case Registration

If a plaintiff files a lawsuit that satisfies the conditions set forth in Article 81 of the Civil Procedure Law (for Trial Implementation) and falls within the scope of case acceptance of the economic division, the economic division shall accept it. In accordance with Article 85 of the Civil Procedure Law (for Trial Implementation), upon receipt of the complaint, the court shall promptly examine it. If the acceptance conditions are met, the case shall be registered within seven days; if the acceptance conditions are not met, the plaintiff shall be notified within seven days, with reasons stated. The period for supplementing or correcting deficiencies in the complaint shall not be calculated within the seven-day period. As for the examination of legal person qualifications, legal representatives, and litigation agents, it may be conducted after case registration; if it is discovered that the case should not have been accepted, a ruling may be made to dismiss the lawsuit.

(2) Cause of Action

Paragraph 1, item (1) of Article 120 of the Civil Procedure Law (for Trial Implementation) provides that the judgment shall state the cause of action.

The cause of action is a summary of the content of the case and a concentrated expression of the nature of the case. Accurately determining the cause of action is an important step in correctly handling a case. The cause of action should be simple and clear, ensuring clear classification, accurate reflection of the dispute, and precise determination of the nature. Adhering to the above principles, the causes of action for economic contract cases shall be classified according to the ten major categories of economic contracts enumerated in the Economic Contract Law, for example: "dispute over quality of a purchase and sale contract," "dispute over compensation under a transportation contract," etc.

For cases involving disputes over oral agreements for immediate settlement between parties for production, exchange, etc., the cause of action may be determined by reference to the above economic contract cases.

If the cause of action at the time of case acceptance differs from that at the time of case closure, the cause of action at case closure shall prevail.

6. Summary Procedure

In accordance with Article 124 of the Civil Procedure Law (for Trial Implementation), basic people's courts and the tribunals dispatched by them shall apply summary procedure to simple economic dispute cases with clear facts, straightforward circumstances, and minor disputes. "Clear facts" means that the parties' statements regarding the disputed facts are substantially consistent, reliable evidence can be provided, and the facts, rights and wrongs, and responsibilities can be determined without extensive investigation; "straightforward circumstances" means that the development process of the dispute involves no complicated or convoluted changes, the focus of the dispute is clear, and the persons and matters involved are not numerous; "minor disputes" means that there are no major principled disagreements between the parties regarding the rights and wrongs, responsibilities, or the subject matter of the action.

For economic dispute cases that begin to be tried under summary procedure, if it is discovered during the trial that the case is not simple, the case may be switched to ordinary procedure. However, simple cases that have already been tried under ordinary procedure shall not be switched to summary procedure.

For economic dispute cases tried under summary procedure, the case file generally shall include: (1) the complaint or the record of an oral complaint; (2) the defense or the record of an oral defense; (3) a power of attorney or certificate; (4) necessary evidence; (5) records of questioning of the plaintiff and defendant; (6) trial (including mediation) records; (7) the judgment, ruling, mediation document, etc.; (8) an execution report; (9) a receipt for litigation costs.

7. Execution Issues

Execution is an important stage in the civil procedure process and a crucial link in ensuring the realization of legally effective judgments, rulings, mediation documents, and other legal documents that, by law, are to be executed by the people's court. Difficulties in execution may be resolved by reference to the following methods.

(1) Through investigation, ascertain the reasons for non-performance, educate the parties on the merits, and contact relevant parties to encourage voluntary performance.

(2) For parties temporarily lacking the ability to pay, with the agreement of the parties through consultation, the payment deadline may be appropriately extended, but the economic responsibility for overdue payment shall be borne; if there are amounts receivable from outside entities, the party shall be ordered to actively recover such debts to repay its own debts.

(3) For parties that have the ability to perform but refuse to perform upon expiration of the deadline, and where ideological education is ineffective, a "Notice of Assistance in Execution" shall be issued to the People's Bank, and measures such as compulsory transfer and allocation shall be taken, or the property shall be sealed up or detained. If, after sealing or detention, the party against whom execution is sought still fails to perform the obligations specified in the legal document within the designated period, the sealed or detained property may be handed over to the relevant unit for sale.

(4) If the property to be executed is located in another locality, the court shall proactively contact the local people's court there and entrust it to carry out the execution. The entrusted people's court shall actively assist in the execution in accordance with Article 165 of the Civil Procedure Law (for Trial Implementation). If, during execution, it discovers that the execution is indeed erroneous, it may submit a written opinion and, with the approval of its president, send a letter requesting the entrusting people's court or its superior people's court to review and handle the matter. During this period, execution shall be suspended.

(5) During execution, if circumstances specified in Articles 182 and 183 of the Civil Procedure Law (for Trial Implementation) arise, a ruling shall be made to suspend or terminate the execution.

(6) If a party applies to the people's court for enforcement of an award made by an arbitration authority pursuant to Article 167 of the Civil Procedure Law (for Trial Implementation), and the people's court finds that the award is indeed erroneous, it shall, with the approval of its president, refuse enforcement and notify the arbitration authority.

(7) When an administrative organ applies to the people's court for compulsory enforcement of an economic sanction decision in accordance with the law, it must submit an application for enforcement, the administrative decision document on which the enforcement is based, and other necessary materials. If the people's court finds that the administrative decision is indeed erroneous, it shall, with the approval of its president, refuse enforcement and notify the administrative organ.
